issue_context.title: Ink-Annotations not shown
issue_context.body:
Attach (recommended) or Link to PDF file here:
[output.pdf](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/files/6374987/output.pdf)

Configuration:
- Web browser and its version: Firefox 88.0
- Operating system and its version: macOS Big Sur 11.2.3 (20D91)
- PDF.js version: 2.8.243
- Is a browser extension: no/Firefox built-in

Steps to reproduce the problem:
1.  add Ink-Annotations to a pdf (i use https://github.com/highkite/pdfAnnotate, Annotations with appearance streams are shown correctly)
2. open output file in firefox

What is the expected behavior? 
The annotations should be visible.
![Bildschirmfoto 2021-04-26 um 09 15 48](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33630884/116043809-6a020f80-a670-11eb-973c-6f2df3dae532.png)

What went wrong? 
The annotations are added to the dom but invisible.
![Bildschirmfoto 2021-04-26 um 09 18 26](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33630884/116043867-7e460c80-a670-11eb-964d-0cc2c6dbfb61.png)

Tested successfull with FoxitReader, AcrobatReader, Chrome and Safari.
comments: The `Ink` annotation doesn't contain an appearance so we should build a default one using the color and the `Inklist`.

Thanks for the fast reply. 
The Ink annotation is already build, but it's transparent.
If i change the stroke manual from transparent to black it is shown like it should.
This is (essentially) just another case of issue #6810.

We draw the annotation on the canvas using the `AP` entry and then we use a transparent line in svg to have an object to interact with in the annotation_layer.
Open your pdf here: https://brendandahl.github.io/pdf.js.utils/browser/#root=997,0 
and you'll see that no appearance stream (AP) is there.
But if you open https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/master/test/pdfs/annotation-caret-ink.pdf in the pdf browser with `#root=25,0`, you'll see an AP entry with some pdf code to render the line.

review_comments: After reading the specs for Ink annotation, I think you forgot to handle dash patterns.

Looking at the PDF document in the issue, it contains a `[3]` dashArray (i.e. the default value) which according to https://www.adobe.com/content/dam/acom/en/devnet/acrobat/pdfs/PDF32000_2008.pdf#G7.3881971 thus would suggest that there should be gaps in the rendered InkAnnotation.

*However*, if you actually look at the rendering and/or Appearance stream that Adobe Reader generates for that PDF document (or even the actual rendering in PDFium), there's *no* dashes present and only solid lines being rendered.
Furthermore, I've tried modifying the reduced test-case included in this patch to specify a non-standard dashArray, and both Adobe Reader and PDFium seem to outright ignore those values and only render the InkAnntations with solid lines.

All-in-all, ignoring the dashArray seems OK in practice here as far as I can tell.

@Snuffleupagus if you want I can try to find usage of dash patterns in my corpus of PDFs, I "just" need a way to detect them (like https://github.com/marco-c/pdf-finder/blob/f045328bbda0bf3a371e992e5c843ba23c02d502/run.py#L20-L37).
